def Target : Prop :=
  ∀ (P D E R : Type) (t : S3 P D E R), t.D23 →
    ∀ w : P → E,
      (∃ p, ∃ o ∈ t.c1 p, ∀ r, t.D22 r → t.c3 o = r ∧ t.c4 r ≠ w p) ∨
      (∃ p, ∃ o ∈ t.c1 p, w p ∉ t.c2 o)

translation: Target defines (names, without asserting or proving) the following proposition. For all arbitrary types P, D, E, and R, and every record t of type S3 P D E R consisting of functions c1 : P → Set D, c2 : D → Set E, c3 : D → R, and c4 : R → E, if t satisfies the hypothesis t.D23, then for every function w : P → E, at least one of two disjuncts holds. Here, the hypothesis t.D23 states: for every r : R that satisfies t.D22 r—meaning there exists some o : D belonging to t.D17 (i.e., o ∈ t.c1 p' for some p' : P) such that t.c3 o = r—the condition t.D21 r holds, namely there exist a function S from the set t.D19 r = {q : P | ∃ o ∈ t.c1 q, t.c3 o = r} to itself and an element p ∈ t.D19 r such that the sets t.D20 p = {e : E | ∃ o ∈ t.c1 p, e ∈ t.c2 o} and t.D20 (S p) = {e : E | ∃ o ∈ t.c1 (S p), e ∈ t.c2 o} have empty intersection (note that in t.D21 r, both S and p are existentially quantified, S is an arbitrary function on t.D19 r, and p and S p are not required to be distinct). Under this hypothesis, for every w : P → E, either: (1) there exist p : P and o ∈ t.c1 p such that for every r : R satisfying t.D22 r (i.e., every r equal to t.c3 o' for some p' : P and o' ∈ t.c1 p'), both t.c3 o = r and t.c4 r ≠ w p hold—note the quantifier order, which requires the single chosen pair (p, o) to satisfy t.c3 o = r and t.c4 r ≠ w p simultaneously for every r with t.D22 r (forcing every such r to equal t.c3 o); or (2) there exist p : P and o ∈ t.c1 p such that w p ∉ t.c2 o (requiring only a single o ∈ t.c1 p excluding w p, not all o ∈ t.c1 p). Nothing requires P, D, E, R, any t.c1 p, any t.c2 o, or t.D17 to be nonempty or finite, and the existential quantifiers over p and o in the two disjuncts are independent.

divergences.description: In the first disjunct, the quantifiers are inverted: Target writes `(∃ p, ∃ o ∈ t.c1 p, ∀ r, t.D22 r → t.c3 o = r ∧ t.c4 r ≠ w p)` instead of `(∀ r, t.D22 r → ∃ p, ∃ o ∈ t.c1 p, t.c3 o = r ∧ t.c4 r ≠ w p)`. Rather than asserting that for every arising inference content `r` there is at least one system `p` and dataset `o ∈ t.c1 p` with content `r` whose inferred experience `t.c4 r` differs from `w p`, the Lean statement demands a single system `p` and single dataset `o ∈ t.c1 p` whose inference content `t.c3 o` simultaneously equals every arising `r`. This makes the first disjunct impossible whenever two distinct inference contents arise (since `t.c3 o` is single-valued) and also false when no datasets arise at all, rendering Target materially different from Proposition 3.7 (and from the author's stated reading) and in fact mathematically false.

True experience is formalized via an arbitrary function `w : P → E`, attaching a single fixed experience to each physical system independent of which dataset `o ∈ t.c1 p` is observed; as the author declares, this notion of true experience is an added modeling idealization not explicitly present in the paper's formalism.

judgement.summary: The formalization is divergent due to a major quantifier inversion in the first disjunct (`∃ p, ∃ o ∈ t.c1 p, ∀ r, ...` instead of `∀ r, ... → ∃ p, ∃ o ∈ t.c1 p, ...`), which forces a single dataset to match every arising inference content simultaneously and makes the formalized proposition false whenever multiple inference contents arise.
